title: fix: libusb_bulk_transfer errors not differentiated — timeout vs. device removal
description:
In src/wp11_ccid.c:298 and 306, any non-zero libusb_bulk_transfer return is mapped to WP11_CCID_ERR_USB. This collapses two meaningfully different conditions:
- LIBUSB_ERROR_TIMEOUT: device is present but slow — caller could retry
- LIBUSB_ERROR_NO_DEVICE: device was physically removed — caller should call slot_remove()
- LIBUSB_ERROR_PIPE: endpoint stall — requires libusb_clear_halt() before retry

Current behavior: all three conditions cause the operation to fail permanently. The caller cannot distinguish 'retry' from 'remove the slot'. A token that takes >1s to sign (common on RSA-2048 operations) will be treated as removed.

Fix:
1. Add WP11_CCID_ERR_TIMEOUT to the error enum
2. Map LIBUSB_ERROR_TIMEOUT → WP11_CCID_ERR_TIMEOUT (retryable)
3. Map LIBUSB_ERROR_NO_DEVICE → WP11_CCID_ERR_NO_CARD (trigger slot removal)
4. Map LIBUSB_ERROR_PIPE → attempt libusb_clear_halt() then WP11_CCID_ERR_USB
5. In the PKCS#11 layer, map WP11_CCID_ERR_TIMEOUT → CKR_DEVICE_ERROR with retry semantics, WP11_CCID_ERR_NO_CARD → trigger hotplug slot_remove

Add comment: 'LIBUSB_ERROR_TIMEOUT is not device removal — do not conflate these. RSA-2048 sign on slow tokens can take >2s.'
